questions.question: What does a Layer 2 switch use to forward frames?

correct.explanation: L2 switches forward using the MAC address (CAM) table.

incorrect.explanation: Routing table reflects a common trap: More switches always mean better routing. Switches extend L2 domains; routing is an L3 function on routers or L3 switches.

incorrect.explanation: DNS cache misses what this question tests. L2 switches forward using the MAC address (CAM) table.

incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting "ACL list" without matching the scenario constraint

answerReview.examTip: On the exam: Expecting an L2 switch to route VLANs — Inter-VLAN routing requires an L3 device — router or L3 switch with SVIs

questions.question: You need to route between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 on one campus switch without an external router. Which device feature applies?
questions.explanation: An L3 switch uses SVIs to route between VLANs locally.

correct.explanation: An L3 switch uses SVIs to route between VLANs locally without an external router.

incorrect.explanation: Port mirroring copies frames to a monitor port for analysis — it does not route traffic between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing traffic capture with inter-VLAN routing

incorrect.explanation: Spanning Tree prevents Layer 2 loops — it does not provide inter-VLAN routing or replace an SVI on a Layer 3 switch.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting STP to route between VLANs

incorrect.explanation: EtherChannel bundles links for bandwidth and redundancy — it is not the feature that routes between VLANs on one campus switch.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using link aggregation where L3 SVI routing is required

answerReview.examTip: Inter-VLAN on one switch without external router → SVI on an L3 switch.
